title: Procedural map generation: an interactive lab built on Herbert Wolverson’s talk
summary: Build a map from the techniques of Herbert Wolverson’s talk, measure it over 200 seeds, and walk it to its exit.

revisions.note: First version, written to test the site's Astro prototype.
Moved to its own project, cj-mills/procedural-map-generation-notes, as the first section of the overhauled notes, and given the old post's URL. The text is unchanged.

Rewritten from the talk's transcript, slides and code: every reference is resolved from a passage in the source library, each claim citing a source was checked by a verifier, and each of our own numbers is regenerated by the build. Adds a note on how the page was checked.

Rebuilt as a map lab covering every technique of the talk: each one a stage of a pipeline you can edit, step through, measure and walk, on one deterministic core, with its traits measured over 200 seeds and checked against the talk’s own code. The cave section’s text is not carried over.
On a phone the map keeps its full width: a step’s references now follow the drawing and its controls, and the controls take less room. The lab has a heading, so the contents list it.

The text is distilled: each rule is a numbered list with a reference a step, tables where versions or modes differ, and what we measured as short items under recurring lead-ins. Eight rule diagrams are drawn by the build. The lab and each step-through open at the size of one step, and open in full when asked, so the page no longer moves as they load. The overworld and zoom maps are drawn as water, grass and mountain, where they were gray.
The lab at the head of the page opens by itself whenever that moves nothing in view, and a closed lab or step-through has a button over its map where it had a link beside its step’s label.
In the lab and each step-through no control moves when it is pressed: the step buttons sit under the map, and the step’s text, whose length changes from step to step, comes after the controls.

The lab at the head of the page opens by itself on every window, in room the page keeps for it from the first paint, so nothing moves as it loads. Open, the lab and each step-through keep one height: stepping, choosing a stage, loading a demo and walking the map no longer move what follows. Each trait’s value is marked on its scale, and the readout comes after the actions.

interactives.description: The map lab: builds a recipe (a pipeline of the talk’s techniques and a seed) with the deterministic core in WebAssembly, steps through the build, measures the pipeline over 200 seeds, and walks the finished level. Mounted once as the lab and once in each technique’s card.
